properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 12 at 10:33PM CDT until October 13 at 11:00PM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

Shoal River Near Crestview affecting Okaloosa County.

For the Shoal River...including Crestview...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring.

* WHERE...Shoal River near Crestview.

* WHEN...Until Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Some flooding of trailers north of the
Okaloosa Correctional Institute. Water surrounds home on Sowel
Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:15 PM CDT Monday the stage was 9.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
Tuesday afternoon and continue falling to 6.8 feet Saturday
evening.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/mob. Click on
the Rivers and Lakes menu for forecasts and observations.

The next statement will be issued when updates occur.

properties.areaDesc: McPherson; Marion; Chase; Reno; Harvey; Butler; Greenwood; Woodson; Allen; Kingman; Sedgwick
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 13 at 2:15AM CDT until October 14 at 10:00AM CDT by NWS Wichita KS
properties.description:
* WHAT...Localized flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, south central, and
southeast Kansas, including the following counties, in central
Kansas, Marion and McPherson. In east central Kansas, Chase. In
south central Kansas, Butler, Harvey, Kingman, Reno and Sedgwick.
In southeast Kansas, Allen, Greenwood and Woodson.

* WHEN...From late this afternoon through mid-morning Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in localized flooding of
rivers, creeks, streams, city streets, underpasses, and other
low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Scattered to numerous thunderstorms with high rainfall rates are
expected to move east to northeast across the same areas late
this afternoon through tonight. Areas of heavy rainfall are
expected, which could lead to localized flooding concerns.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH IN EFFECT FROM LATE THIS AFTERNOON THROUGH MID-MORNING WEDNESDAY

properties.areaDesc: Del Norte Vicinity/Northern San Luis Valley Below 8500 Ft; Alamosa  Vicinity/Central San Luis Valley Below 8500 Ft; Southern San Luis Valley
properties.headline: Freeze Watch issued October 13 at 1:06AM MDT until October 15 at 8:00AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Sub-freezing temperatures as low as 27 possible.

* WHERE...The San Luis Valley.

* WHEN...From late Wednesday night through Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other
sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor
plumbing.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A killing freeze will be possible which could
bring an end to the growing season across the San Luis Valley.
properties.instruction: Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold.

NWSheadline: FREEZE WATCH IN EFFECT FROM LATE WEDNESDAY NIGHT THROUGH THURSDAY MORNING
